questions.q: Which two qualities does Allen say you need to balance to reach your potential?
a: Perspective on the big picture and control of daily details
Ambition for promotion and patience with colleagues
Creativity in planning and discipline in execution
Confidence in decisions and openness to feedback
questions.why: Lesson 1 frames the balance as perspective, seeing the whole, and control, organizing the daily process.

questions.q: What three things does the summary say make daily tasks meaningful?
a: Responsibilities, projects and goals
Meetings, deadlines and rewards
Habits, routines and rest
Clients, managers and budgets
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists identifying responsibilities, grouping tasks into projects and keeping goals in view.

questions.q: What defines a project in Allen’s system?
a: A group of actions leading to a goal you can finish within a year
Any task that takes longer than a single workday
A long-term ambition that takes decades to achieve
A list of responsibilities shared with your team
questions.why: Lesson 2 says projects are the kinds of goals you can complete in under a year, built from smaller actions.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest getting a clear view of your life’s direction?
a: Ask yourself big questions about your ideal future and values
Copy the career path of someone you admire
Focus entirely on this week’s task list
Let your manager set your long-term objectives
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends looking years ahead, imagining your ideal life and asking what you want to be remembered for.

questions.q: What should you do with the list of goals and values you create?
a: Review it often to check that you are on the right track
Lock it away and avoid revisiting it for several years
Share it publicly so others can hold you accountable
Replace it whenever a new opportunity appears
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls the list your elevated view of life and says to review it regularly to stay on course.
